item.title: Report recommends farmland investment trust for PEI
item.description:
Report recommends farmland investment trust for PEI jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/24/2026 - 15:14

A report on agricultural land recommends creating a PEI farmland investment trust to help preserve farmland for agricultural use.

Dr. Greg Keefe’s report entitled Examination of Farmland Trusts looks at models to protect agricultural land and advance opportunities for young farmers in Prince Edward Island.

“The loss of agricultural land is a threat to the social and economic health of the Island. We appreciate Dr. Keefe’s work and valuable insights on a farmland trust, agricultural land use policy and planning, a charitable land trust, environmental farm management and taxation. We will be analyzing his recommendations, with the farmland investment trust being first on the list.”

- Agriculture Minister Hilton MacLennan

Dr. Keefe, an experienced leader in agriculture and veterinary medicine, was engaged by the Department of Agriculture to examine systems to support affordable and stable access to PEI farmland by farmers, especially new farmers. 

The proposed PEI Farmland Investment Trust would buy farmland at market value and lease it to farmers, who would have opportunities to build equity over time and eventually purchase the land.   Investments would be structured to deliver modest returns while supporting sustainable agricultural and keeping PEI farmland under local control.  Management of the farmland and financing for the trust would be handled by a non-governmental organization regulated by government, or by a commission of government. Investment opportunities would be open only to Islanders. 

“Protection of agricultural land, and support for new and existing farmers to own the land they work, are essential for the future of farming in PEI," said Dr. Greg Keefe. "This report contains a series of recommendations, which could help the province to achieve those goals.”

The Examination of Farmland Trusts report is available on the province’s website.

                                                                              

Media contact:

Backgrounder

Dr. Greg Keefe is Professor emeritus and former interim President of UPEI and Dean of the Atlantic Veterinary College. He is the recipient of numerous awards including the Ontario Veterinary College Distinguished Alumni Award and a CVMA award for Advancement of Large Animal Medicine in Canada.

item.title: New rules for non-resident ownership of municipal property
item.description:
New rules for non-resident ownership of municipal property jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/23/2026 - 14:38

Amendments to the Prince Edward Island Lands Protection Act will establish new rules for non-resident ownership of municipal property, effective January 1, 2027. 

Starting in the new year, non-residents will need approval by applying to the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission to acquire more than one municipal property. A municipal property is one acre or less located in an area with an official plan. Until now, these properties have been exempt from the Act.

“These changes mean that all property in Prince Edward Island will now fall under the Lands Protection Act. We will have new rules for non-resident property ownership within municipalities, helping address concerns about vacant properties and supporting housing availability in our communities.”

- Minister of Land and Environment Darlene Compton

These amendments were passed during the spring 2026 sitting of the PEI Legislative Assembly.

For more information on land protection, visit: Lands Protection - Island Regulatory & Appeals Commission.

item.title: New rules improve access for service dog handlers
item.description:
New rules improve access for service dog handlers jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/23/2026 - 13:57

Islanders with service dogs can now voluntarily certify their dogs under a new law, helping to reaffirm their access to public spaces, housing, and services. 

Provincial certification verifies that a service dog meets the training and testing standards in the regulations under the Service Dog Act. The law comes into force on November 29, 2026.

“The goal of this new law is to give service dog handlers more confidence, clarity, and peace of mind about their rights while helping create more welcoming and inclusive communities for everyone. This is great example of how this government works with community members to make positive changes for people living with disabilities.” 

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

Jennifer Sanderson of Summerside, who handles Braden, a Lions Foundation of Canada certified guide dog, says PEI certification will reduce potential conflicts and ease concerns about entering businesses or accessing services. 

“This is exciting for people who use service dogs in PEI,” said Sanderson. “Certification recognizes and validates the vital role that trained service dogs play in supporting their handlers. They are much more than pets, and this helps the public better understand that.”

People can voluntarily certify and register their service dog for free at ResourceAbilities, PEI’s first service dog registrar. They will receive a photo identification card.   

“We’re pleased to serve as PEI’s service dog registrar and to continue working with the province toward our shared goal of removing barriers for people with disabilities,” said executive director of ResourceAbilities Devon Broome. “We look forward to helping Islanders who seek to register their service dogs by making the process clear and accessible.”

Human rights law ensures that people with disabilities have a right to bring service dogs into public places, regardless of certification or registration.

For more information visit: Service Dog Act

item.title: Kindergarten registration opens for the 2027-28 school year
item.description:
Kindergarten registration opens for the 2027-28 school year jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/23/2026 - 10:18

Island parents and guardians can register their child for kindergarten at their local school beginning November 23 for the 2027-28 school year.

Any child who turns five years old by December 31 of the year they begin kindergarten can be enrolled in their local English or French public school. Parents or guardians who are unsure of their local school can contact the Public Schools Branch or La Commission scolaire de langue française for school zone information. 

"Starting kindergarten is an exciting chapter in your child's education and development. I encourage all parents and caregivers to register their child as early as possible. Early registration helps schools plan for the upcoming year and gives children and families more time to get ready for a successful start to kindergarten."

- Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

Parents and guardians can register their child during school hours. They will be required to provide provincially issued identification and proof of address during the registration process.

Families whose child was born outside Canada, or families who speak a first language other than English or French at home are encouraged to first visit the PEI Student Welcome Centre (formally the EAL/FAL reception centre). Staff can assist with the kindergarten registration process by helping parents review required documents and provide guidance to support their child's entry into school.

To help make back to school costs more affordable for families, the province provides free school supplies to Island students from kindergarten to Grade 9.

Learn more about preparing your child for kindergarten at PrinceEdwardIsland.ca/KindergartenRegistration

item.title: Province launches Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign on National Child Day
item.description:
Province launches Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign on National Child Day jenniferdhogan Fri, 11/20/2026 - 15:57

November 20th is National Child Day, an opportunity to recognize and celebrate the contributions of Island children and youth and reaffirm our shared commitment to their safety and well-being. 

As part of that commitment, the province is launching a new public awareness campaign to help Islanders better understand the Duty to Report law. Anyone who knows or suspects that the safety or well-being of a child is endangered must immediately contact Child Protection Services or the police.

“Keeping Island children safe and healthy is a responsibility shared by all of us. If you are concerned about a child, don’t wait. Make the call. Early action can help connect children and families with support.”

-Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

Through multilingual resources, public education sessions, and awareness efforts, the Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign will increase understanding of when and how to report concerns and what happens after a report is made. 

“My department has worked closely with the Department of Social Development and Seniors to ensure policies and procedures across the education and early years systems align with the legal duty to report,” said Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher. “I believe the steps we are taking, including this valuable public education campaign, will improve safety for children across the province.”

With advocacy and support of the Office of the Child and Youth Advocate, the province passed legislation earlier this year that clarifies everyone’s legal responsibility to report concerns about a child’s safety and well-being.

“I welcome the department’s commitment to accepting recommendations from our Office to clarify and strengthen public knowledge regarding the duty to report,” said Marv Bernstein, Child and Youth Advocate. “When we collaborate, we can foster real and meaningful changes that directly uphold the rights of all children and youth to be protected from harm.” 

The 24/7 toll-free child protection phone number is 1 (877) 341-3101. To learn more about reporting, visit: Duty to Report

item.title: Public Schools Branch pilots video cameras on six school buses
item.description:
Public Schools Branch pilots video cameras on six school buses jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/19/2026 - 17:01

The Public Schools Branch (PSB) will begin testing video cameras on six school buses this week to improve safety for students and bus drivers and hold motorists accountable for illegally passing stopped buses.   

The pilot includes exterior cameras that record vehicles passing a stopped school bus while its red lights are flashing, and interior cameras that record video and audio inside the bus. Signs on each bus let riders know that cameras are in use.

"Drivers who pass a stopped school bus are putting children at serious risk," said PSB director of transportation and risk management Dave Gillis. "Our staff report these incidents to police, and we've heard again and again that video evidence would make those reports stronger. This pilot is about keeping everyone who uses our transportation system safe."

The interior cameras will help staff respond to behaviour concerns and incidents on buses fairly and accurately, supporting both students and drivers.

Along with this pilot, the PSB will finalize a policy on the use of video cameras on school buses.

                                                                 

Media contact:
Matt MacLeod
Public Schools Branch
mattimacleod@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder:

How footage is handled

  • Footage is not monitored live and is not reviewed routinely. It is only reviewed when an incident is reported.
  • Only branch-based transportation staff or school administrators may view footage.
  • Footage related to vehicles passing a stopped bus or incidents involving police may be shared with law enforcement as part of the report.
  • External camera footage is automatically deleted after 30 days unless it is needed for a reported incident.
  • Internal camera footage is automatically deleted after 90 days unless it is needed for a reported incident.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator

Government of the Northwest Territories
